title: A quantitative image-based protocol for morphological characterization of cellular solids in feather shafts
protocol: Acquire a series of 2-dimensional micro-images of rachis tissue sections from a localized region of the rachis.
Ensure each micro-image shows clear cellular morphology in each section.
Fix and seal multiple intact tissue sections on the slide from a 100 μm-long localized region of the rachis.
Obtain a stack of qualified micro-images for the entire QMorF protocol.
Mark the reference rachis medulla contour on the display screen for pre-alignment.
Align each tissue section relative to the marked reference contour before acquiring micro-images.
Acquire a micro-image stack of the aligned section slides.
Manually pre-align each rachis tissue section on the microscope slide according to the marked reference medulla contour.
Adjust the position and orientation of each tissue section for proper alignment.
Take bright-field images of the rachis tissue structure using a 10× or 20× objective lens.
Acquire images under transmissive light source with an Olympus BX51 microscope.
Capture images using a Canon EOS 50D digital camera.
Save acquired images as 8-bit monochrome digital images in BMP or uncompressed TIFF format.
Adjust the brightness of the image by tuning the microscope illumination and camera exposure time to enhance object-background contrast.
Process the micro-image of the cross-section rachis tissue using grayscale image complement in MATLAB.
Apply contrast enhancement techniques to the processed images.
Segment the enhanced images to isolate cellular pore patches and mesh networks.
Obtain binary images showing black cellular pore patches isolated by white mesh network borders.
Apply contrast limited adaptive histogram equalization (CLAHE) enhancement method to complement images using the “adapthisteq” toolbox in MATLAB.
Convert complemented grayscale images into black and white images using the “im2bw” toolbox in MATLAB.
Manually remove the cortex portion of the rachis from the binarized image using conventional image processing software.
Remove signals from debris objects from the binarized image using conventional image processing software.
Preserve only image signals contributed by the medulla portion for later stages.
Eliminate small noise patches in the image if their size is below a specified threshold (∼200 μm²).
Apply morphological closing to clarify the pixel patch of each pore structure for accurate elliptical fitting.
Isolate the cellular patch of each pore in the binary image through morphological operations.
Ensure the pre-processed image presents an interconnected mesh network and isolated cellular patches to avoid elliptical-fitting failure.
Apply the edge-finding method (“bwboundaries” toolbox in MATLAB) to identify the edge pixels of each 2D cellular pore patch.
Input 30 randomly sampled edge pixels of a cellular patch into the open source MATLAB module “fit_ellipse.”
The “fit_ellipse” module outputs an ellipse representing the original cellular patch.
Record the position, lengths of the major and minor axes (2a and 2b, respectively), and tilting angle Θ of the ellipse.
Obtain elliptical-fitting object images for every distinguishable cellular pore patch in the pre-processed micro-image stack.
Record parameters that quantify the morphologies of the original cellular pores in each medulla cross-section.
Convert the grayscale micro-image stack into a new stack composed of elliptical-fitting objects.
Coarse-grain average the quantitative characters of elliptical-fitting objects within a grain.
Statistically average parameters and/or calculated results over correctly fitted elliptical objects within a specific coarse-graining volume in the 3D medulla centered at (x, y).
Measure the quantitative morphology at (x, y).
Present the spatial variation of quantitative morphology measurements as a two-dimensional distribution graph called the quantitative morphology field.
Reveal the collective cellular deformation under spatially varying mechanical stress imposed on local cells during morphogenesis.
Align the elliptical-fitting object images in the stack.
Overlap the plural elliptical-fitting object images within a 100 μm-long rachis segment.
Use medulla contour for best manual alignment of each frame.
If tissue section is distorted, use small ROI or fine morphological features as reference coordinates for alignment.
Calculate regional averaged ellipse size PS(x, y) by calculating <πab>.
Obtain regional averaged ellipse elongation rate PEL(x, y) by calculating <a/b>.
Obtain regional averaged ellipse orientation angle PO(x, y) by calculating <Θ>.
